LESSON: AREA

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.2: Area
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Area, part of Measurement in Grade 4 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you work out area of different surfaces?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. pile objects into stacks of cubes and cuboids in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. work out volume of cuboids by piling blocks to form a cuboid,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. calculate the volume of cubes by piling blocks to form a cube,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate use of piling method in working out volume in real life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. pile objects into stacks of cubes and cuboids in real-life situations,

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. work out volume of cuboids by piling blocks to form a cuboid,

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. calculate the volume of cubes by piling blocks to form a cube,

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate use of piling method in working out volume in real life.

   Area helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaboratively compare the area of two surfaces directly by placing one surface on the other,

2. team up with peers while using different unit square cut- outs to cover a given surface,

3. share tasks with peers while counting the number of unit square cut-outs prepared from locally available materials to cover the surface,

4. jointly work with peers to establish that the area of a rectangle or a square is the same as the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns,

5. work out the area of squares and rectangles by multiplying

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaboratively compare the area of two surfaces directly by placing one surface on the other,
2. team up with peers while using different unit square cut- outs to cover a given surface,
3. share tasks with peers while counting the number of unit square cut-outs prepared from locally available materials to cover the surface,
4. jointly work with peers to establish that the area of a rectangle or a square is the same as the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns,
5. work out the area of squares and rectangles by multiplying

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Area together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: learner works independently to calculate the area of squares and

rectangles by multiplying number of rows by the number of columns.

• Digital literacy: learner teams up with others to play games involving the areas of rectangles and squares

using digital resources.

Values:
• Unity: learner works with peers harmoniously to establish that the area of a rectangle or a square is the same

as the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns.

• Integrity: learner gives honest answers while counting the number of unit square cut-outs used to cover the

surface.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education: learner counts the number of unit square cut-outs prepared from locally available

materials to cover the surface.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate counting of the number of unit square cut-outs prepared from locally available

resources to properties of matter in Science and Technology.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. pile objects into stacks of cubes and cuboids in real-life situations,
2. work out volume of cuboids by piling blocks to form a cuboid,
3. calculate the volume of cubes by piling blocks to form a cube,
4. appreciate use of piling method in working out volume in real life.

Remember the key question: How can you work out area of different surfaces?
